segments.text: Nicholas Worth's Oberon operating system running bare metal on a $15 Raspberry Pi. No Linux underneath, no emulation layer. Flash the SD card, plug it in,
and it boots directly into the Oberon graphical desktop in seconds on a Pi 3B, Pi02, or OMX ESP32. A 1980s operating
system designed for minimalism, running on modern hardware, exactly as intended.
The kind of project that exists purely because someone thought it
